settings.aboutTeaser: A poet, translator, and educator, writing in the space between languages — tea, memory, and the stone mill of making something from a life.
settings.aboutLede: I am Ritu Gupta Garg, a poet, translator, and educator who finds beauty in the spaces between languages and cultures.

aboutSections.title: Who I am
aboutSections.body:
My work is deeply influenced by my heritage, my experiences of migration, and the quiet rituals of everyday life.

Born in India and having lived across continents, I write at the intersection of multiple identities. My poetry explores belonging, displacement, memory, and the tender moments that connect us — a cup of tea shared with a loved one, the turning of a stone mill, the rustle of leaves in a forgotten garden.

aboutSections.title: The writing
aboutSections.body:
I write poems, songs, and longer notes. The poems look at identity, language, and the things a family keeps. The longer pieces, on Substack, move from a room or a road toward something quieter.

Poetry is the shortest bridge from the mundane to the spiritual. One has to go through darkness to discover one's own light.

aboutSections.title: Books
aboutSections.body:
Mere Hisse ki Shyaahi (2022) is a personal collection of poems — unspoken emotions, quiet thoughts, and the stories carried within.

The Dance of the Poltergeists (2025) moves through the unseen, where presence feels uncertain and silence has a sound.

aboutSections.title: Translation
aboutSections.body:
As a translator, I believe language can build bridges. My work brings voices from South Asian literature toward English readers, and the other way, keeping the nuances that make each language its own.

Translation, for me, begins with listening. Before a line can cross over, I sit with it until I know what it is holding back — the weight of a single Hindi word, the pause after a couplet, the song hidden inside an ordinary phrase.

Some words refuse to travel. Then the work is not to replace them, but to carry their feeling across, so that a reader on the other side hears the same heartbeat in a different tongue.

aboutSections.title: Teaching
aboutSections.body:
Through teaching I share poetry and translation with students of all ages. Everyone has a story worth telling, and I am glad to help someone find a voice.

A poem does not need big words. It needs one true line, and most people already carry that line inside them. My part is to make the room quiet enough for it to come out.

We read aloud, we write, we cross out, we try again. The aim is never perfection — only the courage to put a feeling on paper and say, this is mine.

aboutSections.title: Tea, woke, chakki
aboutSections.body: The name teapoet.ritu_woke.chakki tells a story of its own. Tea is the quiet ritual. Woke is an engagement with what is happening now. Chakki — the stone mill — is the slow work of taking a raw life and grinding it into something that can be shared.

aboutQuotes.text: Poetry is the art of saying what cannot be said, translating silence into song, and making the invisible visible.

books.title: Mere Hisse ki Shyaahi
books.subtitle: Poetry of emotion and inner voice
books.description: A personal collection of poems that captures unspoken emotions, quiet thoughts, and the stories we carry within. Through simple verses, these pages reflect on pain, love, and self-discovery — written in the ink of one's own truth.
books.authorNote: Not just poetry. A reflection of feelings that often remain hidden.

books.title: The Dance of the Poltergeists
books.subtitle: A dance between presence and absence
books.description: This collection drifts through the unseen — where whispers echo, presence feels uncertain, and reality begins to blur. Through dark, evocative verses, it captures the tension between what is real and what is sensed.
books.authorNote: These poems are disturbances, lingering in the spaces we try not to notice.

poems.title: Words That Speak Beyond Silence
poems.body:
In the world of words, there lives a unique identity—
Ritu Gupta Garg… not just a name, but a beautiful expression.

Every line carries the depth of emotions,
Every poem unfolds a story untold.

At times, she gives voice to silent pain,
At times, she paints joy in the colors of words.

Each phrase born from her pen
Knows the way straight to the heart.

This website is not just a platform,
But a graceful world of feelings—
Where every word holds truth,
And every poem feels alive.

poems.title: Whispers in the Tea Garden
poems.body:
Among the rustling leaves of green
Where morning light breaks through unseen
I find the words I cannot speak
In every breath, the truth I seek

poems.title: The Weight of Words
poems.body:
Each syllable a feather falls
Upon the silence of these walls
Translation is a tender art
Of bridging minds and touching hearts

poems.title: Chakki Dreams
poems.body:
The old stone mill turns round and round
With ancient rhythm, ancient sound
My grandmother's hands, so wise and worn
Ground stories into every morn

writings.title: A Coun-trees
writings.excerpt: A country of trees. At Wah Lodge, Kandbari, the spartan quiet unwinds an overworked life and makes you feel like one of the trees.
writings.content:
Wah Lodge at Kandbari, Palampur offers a rare mix of grounding and centering to the overstimulated energies of the mind, body, and soul. Its spiritual appeal lies in offering the luxury of austere living.

It was a homestay, but became a home — a hammock, as if one end is tied to a mountain peak and the other to the root of a tall pine.

Trees were a poetree. The deodar and cedar, the pine — tall vertical roads between sky and earth.

writings.title: Kenopsia
writings.excerpt: Kenopsia is a painful joy sometimes, and other times a longing — the quiet of a fort, not the quiet of a spa.
writings.content:
Kenopsia is a painful joy sometimes, and other times a desirable element, a longing even, to be part of something that has already gone.

After a grand wedding at Taj Aravalis, and stays at Rohet Garh and a palace at Mount Abu, the empty royal corridors felt less sepulchral than cultural — a quiet pregnant with the sound of gallops.
